transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Yeah, um… thanks. I guess I came in because I’ve been having a hard time not… beating myself up, I suppose.

It’s mostly about work. I keep feeling like I’m not really “senior” material, like maybe I somehow convinced people I could handle more than I actually can. I know that probably sounds a little dramatic, and I’m still getting things done, but it’s been sitting with me a lot and I thought maybe I should talk to someone before I make too much of it.
Did these feelings start after a specific change or event at work?

Yeah, I think so. It wasn’t like one big dramatic thing, but I started noticing the ups and downs maybe about a month ago, after they asked me to cover the senior analyst duties. I mean, I’m managing, but that seems to be when it really started feeling noticeable.
Do these feelings mostly come up when you’re thinking about work or doing your senior duties?

Mostly, yeah. It’s tied to work… especially when I’m doing the senior analyst stuff or even just thinking about it afterward.

I start telling myself I’m not really senior material, like I somehow fooled everyone into thinking I could handle more than I actually can. I know that probably sounds harsher than I mean it, but… that’s kind of the loop I get stuck in.
Outside of work, do you still find yourself beating yourself up in the same way?

Not really in the same way, no. I mean, I can be hard on myself generally, but the thing that’s been bothering me is mostly this work piece… like I keep telling myself I’m not actually senior material, or that I somehow fooled everyone into thinking I can handle more than I can.

I know that probably sounds a bit much, but that’s the main way it shows up.
Have these feelings made it harder for you to do your job?

A little, yeah… I mean, I’m still getting to work and getting things done, so I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. But I’ve noticed I’m double-checking myself more than usual, like I don’t quite trust my judgment.

And, I guess outside of work I’ve pulled back some from friends and family too, just because I’m not totally sure where my head’s at lately. Does that make sense?
If the senior analyst duties were taken away tomorrow, do you think this self-doubt would mostly go away?

I think… mostly, yeah. Or at least it would get a lot quieter.

The thing I came in for is really that I keep beating myself up over the senior part — like I’m not actually senior material, and I somehow fooled people into thinking I can handle more than I can. So if those duties were gone, I’d probably feel less exposed, I guess.

I don’t want to make it sound like I’m blaming the job title for everything, but… yeah, that seems to be where most of that self-doubt is coming from.
In the past month, have you found yourself worrying a lot about several different areas of your life, not just work?

I don’t think so, not several different areas. I mean, I’ll worry about normal stuff, like anyone does, but the thing that keeps looping is mostly work and whether I’m handling the senior responsibilities okay.

I’m not sure if I’m answering that the right way, but no, I wouldn’t say it’s been a lot of worrying across my whole life.
Over the past month, have you been feeling down or depressed most days?

Yeah… I guess I have, most days. I don’t know if I’d call it depressed-depressed, but there’s been this heavy, low feeling lately.

It’s like I’m getting through work and home and doing what I’m supposed to do, but everything feels kind of muted… like the color’s turned down, if that makes sense.
Over the past month, have you been enjoying things less than usual?

Yeah… maybe a little less, I guess.

I mean, I usually look forward to simple stuff on the weekend — grilling, maybe going fishing, or just putting on a record and relaxing. Lately I’ll kind of think about doing it, but then the grill stuff just sits there, or the records sit there, and I don’t really care enough to start.

It’s not like I’m incapable of enjoying anything, but… yeah, it’s been less than usual, I’d say. Does that make sense?
Over the past month, have you had thoughts that you’d be better off dead or of hurting yourself?

Um… I don’t want to worry you. I haven’t made any kind of plan to hurt myself or anything like that.

But… yeah, sometimes I catch myself thinking it might be easier if I just didn’t wake up one morning. It feels bad saying that out loud. I’m not trying to do anything, it’s more like the thought just shows up. Does that make sense?
When you’re not thinking about work, do you still feel that same heavy, low mood?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, work definitely adds to it, but even when I’m just at home or it’s the weekend, it’s still kind of there.

Not dramatic or anything, just this heavy, low feeling most days lately… like I’m going through the motions and everything’s a bit duller than it should be. Is that what you mean?
Has this heavy, low mood been present for at least two weeks?

Yeah… I think it’s definitely been more than two weeks.

I was kind of hoping it was just a rough patch, but looking back, these low, guilty stretches have been hanging around off and on for… maybe about eleven months now. Not constant every single minute, but it keeps coming back. Is that the kind of timeframe you mean?
During those eleven months, have there been stretches of at least a couple of months when your mood felt mostly back to normal?

Um… I don’t think there’s been a full couple of months where I felt totally back to myself, no.

There might be better weeks here and there, where I can kind of function and seem okay, but looking back, the low, guilty feeling has been hanging around off and on for about eleven months. I wish I could say there was a clear break, but… I’m not sure there really was. Does that answer it?
Have you been feeling this low mood on and off for at least two years?

No, I don’t think it’s been two years. Looking back, it’s more like these low, guilty periods have been coming and going for about eleven months.

I mean, that’s still a while, but not two years… if I’m counting it right.
During these past eleven months, was there ever a stretch of at least two months when you had no depression symptoms at all?

I don’t think there was a full two-month stretch with no symptoms at all, no.

There were definitely times that were better, and I could sort of tell myself I was okay, but looking back… the low, guilty periods were still hanging around off and on through the past eleven months. I hope that’s the kind of answer you’re asking for.
Over this past month, have you been sleeping noticeably more or less than usual?

Yeah… a little, I guess. It’s not like I’m not sleeping at all, but I’ve been waking up way too early sometimes, already thinking about client tickets, and then I can’t really get back to sleep.

Other nights I technically get enough hours, but I still wake up feeling worn out. I don’t know if that counts as “noticeably,” but it’s been happening.
Over the past month, have you been feeling tired or low on energy most days?

Yeah… I think so, most days, but I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is.

It’s more like by the time I get home from the office, even little things—checking the mail, loading the dishwasher—feel like they take more effort than they should. I can still do them, usually, but it feels heavier than it ought to, if that makes sense.
Over the past month, has your appetite been noticeably less or more than usual?

A little less, I think. I mean, I’m still eating, but some evenings I’ll just grab a few bites of something or skip supper if I’m not really feeling hungry.

It’s not dramatic or anything, but my belt has been a bit looser lately, and I’m not trying to lose weight. So… yeah, I guess my appetite’s been off.
Before this past eleven months, was there ever another time in your life when you felt depressed like this for at least two weeks?

I’m not sure, honestly. I mean, I’ve had rough patches before, like anyone, but I don’t know that I’d call them the same as this or say they clearly lasted two weeks.

Nothing really stands out to me as a definite “yes,” if that makes sense.
Have you ever had a period where your mood was unusually high, energetic, or irritable for several days in a row?

I guess… yes, there have been times like that before this low stretch. I wouldn’t say I was out of control or anything, but for several days I felt almost too sure of myself, like more keyed up or confident than normal.

And I got irritated more easily than I’d like to admit—snapping at people over little things, like a slow email or a client asking the same question twice. I know that probably doesn’t sound great, but it was noticeable for me.
